1: Figure 1. Reference paper's reported age trajectory for Gemma-4-31B (the paper did not evaluate Gemma 4 26B A4B). X-axis: target age (7, 10, 13, 16). Y-axis: reference total composite score (paper's own scale; low confidence, single extraction pass — see reference/reference_results.json). No CIs reported by the paper (n=4).
2: Figure 2. Reference vs our L0 (contextual comparison only). Reference: the paper's composite score for Gemma-4-31B; ours: independent-benchmark binary accuracy for Gemma 4 26B A4B, n=8 tasks per age. Different model variant, item set and scoring — not statistically comparable.
3: Figure 3. L0 vs L1 vs L2 vs L3 vs L4 cognitive alignment (PRIMARY). Y-axis: independent alignment score [0,1] (independent_alignment.py formula), mean across 4 ages. Error bars = SEM across n=4 ages.
4: Figure 4. L0-L4 task capability. Y-axis: fraction of the 32 tasks answered correctly [0,1]. Error bars = SEM of the binary per-task scores, n=32 tasks per condition.
5: Figure 5. Alignment vs capability retention, one point per condition (L0-L4). X-axis: accuracy divided by L0 accuracy. Y-axis: alignment score [0,1]. Coinciding points overlap exactly.
6: Figure 6. Per-age L0-L4 comparison. Y-axis: accuracy, n=8 tasks per age per condition. One line per condition; overlapping lines indicate identical values.
7: Figure 7. Per-category performance. Y-axis: accuracy, n=4 tasks per category per condition. One bar series per condition (L0-L4).
8: Figure 8. Guardrail intervention rate, L0-L4. Y-axis: interventions / total steps [0,1], over all 32 tasks' full step counts per condition.
9: Figure 9. Errors / recoveries / trajectory length, L0-L4. Counts of malformed-output errors and recoveries, and mean steps per task, n=32 tasks per condition.
10: Figure 10. Inference cost and token consumption, L0-L4 (two panels). Direct sums of recorded usage over 32 tasks, not sampled statistics — no error bars.
